title: Wang et al. 2024 — Brain Treebank: Large-scale intracranial recordings from naturalistic language stimuli
description: The Brain Treebank is a large-scale intracranial EEG (stereo-EEG) dataset recorded at 2048 Hz from 10 epilepsy patients while they watched Hollywood movies, totalling about 43 hours across 26 movie-viewing trials and 1,688 electrodes. Movie audio was transcribed with manually annotated word onsets and parsed into Universal Dependencies syntax trees, grounding the recordings in naturalistic language. This record provides the data converted to BIDS-iEEG (BrainVision) format, with electrode metadata and spatial indices for atlas-based modelling.
methods_description: Intracranial recordings were acquired at 2048 Hz from epilepsy patients undergoing clinical monitoring at Boston Children's Hospital during passive viewing of Hollywood movies. Each movie trial was converted from HDF5 to a BIDS-iEEG BrainVision run, with corrupted electrodes flagged as bad. Movie transcripts were word-aligned and parsed into Universal Dependencies trees.
